title: Rav Yitzchak bar Avin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman considers Yuchasin’s placement of him in Rabbah’s time correct: Kiddushin 77a has Rabbah explaining “which chalalah is mentioned,” followed by Rav Yitzchak bar Avin’s explanation of “mentioned,” etc. In Zevachim 42a he says, “For example, where he rendered it piggul”; “if so, what is the Rabbis’ reason?” Rava said, etc. Hyman infers that Rava explains his words, while he explains Rabbah’s; Rosh Hashanah 17a likewise has Rava adding to his words.

Hyman also lists Ketubot 45b, Bava Kamma 76a, Shevuot [printed בו.], and Bekhorot 38a. Hyman characterizes these as halakhic discussions in which Yitzchak explains earlier statements. A matching passage is found at Shevuot 26a.

notes.text: The supplied Shevuot folio בו. is irregular and remains unresolved; no folio 2 is substituted. The chronology is Hyman’s inference from who explains whom.

The whole saved Davidson Shevuot26a scalar explicitly names full Rav Yitzchak bar Avin interpreting the oath verse. This is a matching candidate beside supplied בו., not proof of a bet/kaf error or authorization to erase the literal locator. Hyman AFFIRMS Yuchasin’s Rabbah-era placement and infers chronology from Rava explaining him and his explaining Rabbah; this is attributed rather than independently dated. Zevachim’s שפיגל is an active verb, rendered it piggul, not merely a noun. Earlier Kiddushin/Zevachim/RoshHashanah occurrences are inherited, not newly inspected full folios. All full Rav titles remain.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 787) gives the irregular Shevuot locator בו. The consulted Shevuot 26a names Rav Yitzchak bar Avin interpreting the oath verse. Kiddushin 77a has him explain Rabbah’s statement, and Zevachim 42a has him discuss piggul during slaughter before Rava’s reply. In the consulted Rosh Hashanah 17a, Ketubot 45b, Bava Kamma 76a and Bekhorot 38a he is called Rabbi. Ketubot 45b also gives an alternative attribution to Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba. Hyman’s chronology and his agreement with Yuchasin remain his assessment.
